# lol.trq.alts

> A consumer-agnostic account library for Minecraft: Java Edition, for launchers, tools, the host applications of bots, and account managers. Sign-in by Microsoft browser login (PKCE), device code, OAuth refresh token, cookie text, cookie file, session token, or offline, with silent renewal of a stored session; account management over a token (profile, entitlements, name, skin, cape, attributes, chat-signing certificate, blocklist) and anonymous profile lookup; paced bulk operations; an encrypted local store with an optional host-supplied key; per-account proxy routing; a shared vault on the Alt Vault Protocol 0.5 with client-side encryption and verification; and async avatar and game-stats caches. Pure JDK plus Gson, Java 25, with no Minecraft or renderer types of its own.

Current version: 1.0.0. Coordinate: `com.github.trq-lol:lol.trq.alts` on JitPack, with the release tag (`v1.0.0`) as the version. Gson is an ordinary `api` dependency that a host receives transitively. The jar is the named module `lol.trq.alts` (a `module-info.java`; no `Automatic-Module-Name`), which `requires transitive com.google.gson`, exports the twelve API packages and nothing under `lol.trq.alts.internal`, and is sealed. The exported API is frozen for 1.x by a committed dump, `api/lol.trq.alts.api`, which the build checks.

The library is host-agnostic. A host supplies a few seams from `lol.trq.alts.spi` (session injection, storage directory, main-thread executor and notifications are required; texture upload, avatar source, stats source, proxy provider and store key provider are optional, and a device-code prompt is passed per sign-in) and builds one `AltsRuntime` through its `Builder`. The runtime owns everything it builds: an `AccountStore` (`alts.store()`) and a `HostSecrets` (`alts.secrets()`) on the host's directory, a transport with the host's proxy provider, and an executor (the host's, or one it creates). Nothing is process-wide, so two runtimes on two directories share nothing, and each store file is locked to one runtime: a second runtime on the same directory fails `build()` with `CONFLICT`. `build()` loads the stores, so `alts.store().accounts()` is populated as soon as it returns. `AltsRuntime` is `AutoCloseable`: `close()` flushes and unlocks the stores, closes the transport, shuts down an executor it created, and ends whatever still waits on the runtime. Microsoft login takes the host's own Azure client id; the library ships no default, and `MicrosoftAuthConfig.legacyMsa` speaks the pre-Azure MSA dialect.

Every failure is an `AltsFailure` (in `lol.trq.alts`): a `kind()` from the one enum `AltsFailure.Kind` (`NETWORK`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `UNAUTHORIZED`, `REAUTH_REQUIRED`, `NOT_ENTITLED`, `NOT_FOUND`, `XBOX_DENIED`, `DECLINED`, `TIMED_OUT`, `CANCELLED`, `INVALID_INPUT`, `CONFLICT`, `NOT_CONFIGURED`, `STORAGE`, `CRYPTO`, `PROTOCOL`, `UNKNOWN`), a message the library builds, the stated wait (`retryAfter()`, `retryAt()`), the decoded Xbox Live refusal (`xstsError()`), and `retryable()`. A result a host branches on (`LoginResult`, `AccountStatus`, `NameChangeResult`, `ProfileCreationResult`, `ClaimResult`, `BulkEntryResult`) carries it as `Optional<AltsFailure> failure()`; everything else throws the unchecked `AltsException`, and a library future completes exceptionally with nothing else. A host branches on the kind, never on the message. A refused credential, an unreachable service and a rate limit are always classified apart.

`AltLoginService` is the whole sign-in surface: seven routes (`loginMicrosoft`, `loginDeviceCode`, `loginRefreshToken`, `loginCookie`, `loginCookieFile`, `loginSession`, `loginOffline`) plus `loginAccount`, which reuses a stored session while it is live and otherwise renews it from the account's refresh token, and `routed(tag)`, a view whose requests carry a route tag for the proxy provider. Every route returns a `LoginResult` and never throws at the caller. The device-code flow and the cookie chain were tested against loopback and scripted servers only, not against the live services.

`AltAccountService` (`check`, `refresh`) validates and renews a stored account without installing a session; `check` is read-only, and is the one to use when only looking, because the token endpoint rotates the refresh token on every redemption. `AccountStatus.State` is `VALID`, `RENEWED`, `EXPIRED`, `REAUTH_REQUIRED`, `NOT_ENTITLED` (which includes an Xbox Live refusal), `UNREACHABLE` (an outage or a rate limit; the failure's kind tells them apart) or `UNKNOWN`.

`lol.trq.alts.account` is the surface over a live token, reached as `alts.accountServices(account)`: the full profile (and creating one for an entitled account that has none), entitlements as a product set, name availability, eligibility, change and a scheduled claim, skin and cape changes (with local skin validation), player attributes and platform ban status, the chat-signing certificate, and the blocklist. None of it installs a session or touches the store. A read throws `AltsException`; a mutation whose refusal is an ordinary outcome returns a classified result. `alts.profileLookup()` resolves a player by name or UUID with no token, ten names per request for a list. `Builder#accountEndpoints` points both at another base.

`lol.trq.alts.bulk` runs `checkAll`, `refreshAll`, `entitlementsAll` and `importCredentials` over many accounts with bounded concurrency, spacing between starts, a retry budget that only retries transient failures, per-entry progress, and cancellation. A rate limit, with or without a stated wait, stops the run by default or pauses it when the host opts out of stopping. Every entry is reported, a run cut short reporting the rest as `CANCELLED`. Result labels are usernames or positional (`entry 4`) and never the input line.

Requests leave through the runtime's transport and nowhere else: finite timeouts, a 1 MiB cap on JSON and text bodies, no redirect following except a bounded, credential-stripping one for images, header checks (no control characters, no caller-set `Proxy-Authorization`), and the runtime's `ProxyProvider`, which receives a `NetworkScope` (purpose, account, route tag) and returns a `ProxyRoute`. Proxy resolution fails closed. An HTTPS target behind an HTTP proxy is tunnelled by the library, which sends the proxy credential on the `CONNECT` only and keeps connections apart per proxy identity; the JVM still resolves the target host name locally on that path. All blocking work runs on the runtime's executor (a virtual thread per task, or the host's executor), never on the common pool.

The stores (`AccountStore`, `HostSecrets`) are AES-256-GCM files written atomically with a rolling backup and coalesced for 100 ms; `flush()` writes at once. The default key is derived from machine properties and is obfuscation; a `StoreKeyProvider` supplies real key material, for that runtime only. A file that cannot be read is never treated as empty or written over: it is reported on `loadError()` (kind `STORAGE`), copied aside to `<name>.unreadable.<time>`, and every write is refused until a load succeeds or the host calls `discardUnreadable()`. Under a provider the machine-derived key is accepted only on a launch that sets `migrateFromMachineKey(true)`.

The shared vault (`lol.trq.alts.vault`) implements the Alt Vault Protocol (AVP) 0.5, a draft specification, as a client. A repository's owner holds keys derived from a 24-word BIP39 phrase (`OwnerIdentity`) and signs every change to the members, the refresh-token policy and the hosts; every write is a member-signed commit; the client verifies the chain from genesis and every commit itself, pins the highest verified state, wraps the data key only to keys from an invite token, and fails the whole operation with `PROTOCOL` on a forged state or a rollback. `alts.vault()` connects to hosts by key on the runtime's transport, `SharedVault` is one member device's copy, `VaultSnapshot` is the state a host persists encrypted, and refresh tokens are withheld unless the owner turns sharing on. It does not resist denial of service, metadata exposure, a member who is the attacker, or a withholding host; SECURITY.md states the full model. `LegacyVaultReader` reads a 0.4 repository once, read-only, so its accounts can move to a new one.

Notes for implementers: the library never imports a host type, and it must never name a specific consuming application, product, or sponsor, or another authentication library or tool, in source, docs, tests, or commits. Implementation lives under `lol.trq.alts.internal`, which is never exported and which no exported signature may name; `apiCheck` enforces the dump and `./gradlew apiDump` records an intended addition. DTOs are Java records with a `@SerializedName` on every component, and the ones that carry credentials override `toString` to redact them. Failure messages never repeat a transport exception's own text. Test seams are package-private and need no system property: each test builds and closes its own runtime, store or transport, and `check` runs the suite on the class path and again on the module path. House style is palantir-java-format (4-space, 120 column); run `./gradlew spotlessApply` before committing and `./gradlew check` to gate. Every multi-line Java snippet in the getting-started guide is inlined from a compiled example, so change the example first and the guide second.

## Documentation

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/README.md): Overview, features, installation, and quick start.
- [Getting started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/docs/GETTING_STARTED.md): Wiring the seams, every sign-in route, the error kinds, account management, lookup, bulk runs, proxies, the store key, closing the runtime, and the shared vault end to end.
- [Architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): Layers, the module and internal packages, threading, store persistence, transport rules, the error model, bulk runs, and the AVP 0.5 client.
- [Agent guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/CLAUDE.md): The mental model, the patterns that matter, and the pitfalls, written for coding agents.
- [Examples](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/examples/README.md): The compiled samples the guide inlines from.
- [Changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/CHANGELOG.md): Release history; the 1.0.0 section opens with the migration from 0.12 and the table from every former failure constant to its kind.
- [Security policy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/SECURITY.md): How to report a vulnerability, and the threat model for the stores, the transport, tokens in logs, sign-in, the AVP 0.5 vault, and the module boundary.

## Design records

- [Refresh-token design](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/docs/specs/2026-07-28-refresh-token-auth.md): Shipped. Why renewal, the sharing policy, and the typed failure are shaped the way they are.
- [Alt-management surface design](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/docs/specs/2026-08-05-alt-management-surface.md): Shipped across 0.8.0 to 0.12.0. Per-account proxies, operating on an account without logging into it, UUID-keyed avatars, entitlement as an outcome, bulk operations, and device-code login.
- [Account management and the 1.0 surface](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/docs/specs/2026-08-06-account-management-1.0.md): The account services, shipped in 0.11.0 and 0.12.0 and finalized in 1.0.0.
- [The 1.0 freeze](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/docs/specs/2026-11-12-1.0-freeze.md): Accepted. Runtime-owned state, one error model, the internal package with the module descriptor and the API gate, and the vault on AVP 0.5, with the decisions and the type inventory.

## Core source

- [AltsRuntime](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/AltsRuntime.java): The wiring root and its builder; the one object a host constructs, owns and closes.
- [AltsFailure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/AltsFailure.java): The one failure value and its `Kind` enum, with what each kind means and `retryable()`.
- [AltsException](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/AltsException.java): The one exception, carrying an `AltsFailure`.
- [module-info](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/module-info.java): The exported packages, the Gson requirement, and the two packages opened to Gson.
- [API dump](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/api/lol.trq.alts.api): Every exported type, member and signature, as the compatibility gate checks them.
- [AltLoginService](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/auth/AltLoginService.java): The sign-in interface every route lives on, and the routed view.
- [LoginResult](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/auth/LoginResult.java): A sign-in's account or its failure.
- [AltAccountService](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/auth/AltAccountService.java): Checking and renewing a stored account without logging into it.
- [AccountStatus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/auth/AccountStatus.java): What an account is worth right now, as a state a host can branch on.
- [MicrosoftAuthConfig](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/auth/MicrosoftAuthConfig.java): Host-supplied client id, endpoints, and the OAuth vs legacy-MSA dialect.
- [CookieFile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/auth/CookieFile.java): Reading an exported cookie file, byte-order-mark aware and size-capped.
- [XstsError](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/auth/XstsError.java): The Xbox XErr codes decoded, so a refusal says what to fix.
- [DeviceCodePrompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/spi/DeviceCodePrompt.java): The seam that shows a device-code challenge, and the phishing rule that comes with it.
- [AccountServices](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/account/AccountServices.java): The surface over a token: profile, entitlements, name, skin, cape, attributes, certificates, blocklist.
- [AccountEndpoints](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/account/AccountEndpoints.java): Another base for the account services and the profile lookup.
- [ProfileService](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/account/ProfileService.java): The profile read, the read that treats a missing profile as empty, and profile creation.
- [NameService](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/account/NameService.java): Availability, eligibility, change, and the scheduled claim.
- [SkinService](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/account/SkinService.java): Skin changes, with local validation before upload.
- [SkinProblem](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/account/SkinProblem.java): Why bytes are not an uploadable skin.
- [PlayerAttributes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/account/PlayerAttributes.java): Privileges, preferences and platform ban status.
- [CertificateService](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/account/CertificateService.java): The chat-signing key pair.
- [ProfileLookupService](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/account/ProfileLookupService.java): Anonymous lookup by name, UUID, or a list of names.
- [Entitlements](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/account/Entitlements.java): What an account owns, as a product set and not a boolean.
- [BulkOperations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/bulk/BulkOperations.java): Checking, refreshing, reading entitlements of, and importing many accounts.
- [BulkOptions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/bulk/BulkOptions.java): Concurrency, spacing, retry budget, stopping on a rate limit, and the route tag.
- [CredentialKind](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/bulk/CredentialKind.java): What a pasted line is taken to be, and why it never guesses.
- [ProxyProvider](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/spi/ProxyProvider.java): The per-request routing seam, and why it fails closed.
- [NetworkScope](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/net/NetworkScope.java): What a request is for: purpose, account, route tag.
- [ProxyRoute](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/net/ProxyRoute.java): Direct, HTTP (with or without credentials) or SOCKS5, with a redacting `toString`.
- [AccountStore](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/store/AccountStore.java): The account store, its mutators, its lock, its load and save reporting, and `discardUnreadable()`.
- [HostSecrets](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/store/HostSecrets.java): The per-user secrets, kept apart from the accounts, on the same terms.
- [StoreKeyProvider](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/spi/StoreKeyProvider.java): The host-supplied store key seam and its fail-closed rules.
- [AltAccount](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/model/AltAccount.java): The stored account record, its copy methods, and its redacting `toString`.
- [AsyncCache](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/cache/AsyncCache.java): The lazy, non-blocking, stale-while-revalidate, bounded cache.
- [AvatarSource](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/spi/AvatarSource.java): The face-fetch seam; the default crops from Mojang so no third party sees the account list.
- [SkinAvatarCache](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/skin/SkinAvatarCache.java): UUID-keyed avatar cache with bounded downloads and retry on backoff.
- [TimeSource](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/time/TimeSource.java): The corrected-clock seam the scheduled claim reads.
- [VaultHosts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/vault/VaultHosts.java): The runtime's way to AVP 0.5 hosts, matched by key, and the first-contact rule.
- [SharedVault](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/vault/SharedVault.java): One member device's copy of a repository: create, join, resume, write, sync, and the owner's operations.
- [SyncReport](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/vault/SyncReport.java): What a sync found: new states, divergence, a policy change, unreadable heads, pending leaves.
- [VaultSnapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/vault/VaultSnapshot.java): The secret state a host persists: the pin, the retained keys, the merged accounts.
- [OwnerIdentity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/vault/OwnerIdentity.java): The owner keys from a BIP39 phrase or its entropy.
- [LinkSession](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/vault/LinkSession.java): Linking a second owner device after a confirmation code.
- [VaultIdentity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/vault/VaultIdentity.java): The member identity, its passphrase-wrapped and recovery forms, and the guarded 0.4 challenge signer.
- [RepoLocator](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/vault/RepoLocator.java): The token an owner gives a joiner; `InviteToken`, `LinkRequest` and `LinkGrant` sit beside it.
- [LegacyVaultReader](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trq-lol/lol.trq.alts/main/src/main/java/lol/trq/alts/vault/LegacyVaultReader.java): The read-only importer for a 0.4 repository.

## Protocol

- [Alt Vault Protocol (AVP)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trqlmao/avp/main/SPEC.md): The vendor-neutral wire standard this library's shared vault implements, at version 0.5.
